description: Commissioned by UN Women, Bystander is a tense, intimate short film exploring the split second where instinct, fear and responsibility collide. Across a series of everyday settings - a bus stop late at night, a locker room after a match, an online gaming session, an open-plan office - we witness subtle but recognisable moments of harassment and boundary-crossing behaviour directed towards women. Nothing heightened. Nothing dramatised beyond reality. Just the familiar discomfort of something not quite right. Each character faces the same internal question: intervene, or stay silent? Told through restrained performances, tightening frames and immersive sound design, the film places the audience inside the pause before action, where rationalisation and conscience wrestle for control. Rather than judging its characters, Bystander examines the psychology of inaction in the face of harassment and abuse towards women and the quiet realisation that silence, too, has consequences. This  professional campaign titled 'BYSTANDER' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: UN Women UK, by ad agency: Media Trust. description: Did you spot all these cameos in 'What has the BBC ever done for me?' A skeptical viewer questions the value of the BBC, leading to a journey through iconic shows, programs, and radio services. This fast-paced exploration highlights the breadth of BBC content, from news and drama to nature documentaries and entertainment, while examining the corporation's overall impact on British culture and the economy. Romesh Ranganathan is asking the big question, ‘What has the BBC ever done for me?’ He begins by asking a star-studded Queen Vic pub, complete with Coldplay’s Chris Martin on piano. Romesh travels through Albert Square, Casualty, BBC News, Radio 1Xtra, Graham Norton’s studio, Wimbledon, ending up on stage in Strictly Come Dancing. Along the way he meets Claudia Winkleman and some Traitors, Alan Carr, Daleks, Ruth Jones as Gavin & Stacey’s Nessa, Hey Duggee and Anton Du Beke. There is a BBC for each of us, funded by all of us. This is our BBC. This  professional campaign titled 'What has the BBC ever done for me?' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: BBC, . description: Confused.com and Leo UK are bringing some of the nation’s most familiar sayings to life in a new campaign capturing the disproportionately good feeling of having Just Used Confused.com. ‘Feels like…’ is the latest chapter of the award-winning brand platform, which celebrates the fleeting sense of triumph that comes from conquering life admin, saving some money and feeling, briefly, like a fully functioning adult. The 2025 instalment of the platform won multiple Golds at Creative Circle and British Arrows, including the prestigious John Webster Award. Each film begins in the real world as someone finishes sorting their insurance with Confused.com. Their relief triggers a comedic cutaway into a heightened world where the feeling is expressed through a familiar idiom, interpreted very literally by a cast of handcrafted animal puppets. The environments and supporting characters were developed and enhanced with AI production tools. In ‘The Cat That Got the Cream’, a man sorting his car insurance cuts to an ageing, bespectacled cat in a supermarket. After seriously considering whether he deserves a pot of cream, the cat drops it into his basket and reasons: “Cream, double cream! That’s coming home with me that, Meow.” ‘Laughing ’til the Cow Comes Home’ introduces Pig and Sheep, two laid-back former university housemates enjoying an afternoon of doing very little while Cow is at his nine-to-five. Pig is midway through a joke when Cow appears in the doorway, briefcase in hand, and shouts: “Oh please don’t stop on my account...” Completing the trio is ‘The Early Bird That Got the Worm’, starring a polished and profoundly pleased-with-herself blue tit. Carrying a shopping bag emblazoned with a worm, she struts past a queue of less fortunate birds and announces: “you should’ve set your alarms”. The characters were developed with BlinkInk stop motion directing duo, Andy Biddle and Adeena Grubb, with every detail designed to build their personalities, from the cat’s increasingly necessary reading glasses to Cow’s carefully pressed workwear, and the early bird’s jumper draped deliberately over her shoulders. Biddle was a lead animator on Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs, while Grubb is a multi-award-winning puppet maker and animation director. Their combined experience in handcrafted filmmaking helped bring the campaign’s familiar idioms to life through characters packed with charm, wit and sharply observed detail. Each film ends with the line, “Insurance feels better when you’ve just used Confused.com”, followed by the familiar Confused.com whistle, performed by its respective puppet character. First introduced with the launch of the ‘Just Used Confused.com’ platform, the whistle has since grown into an established sonic asset for the brand. The campaign will be supported by ten and six second edits, alongside radio and social activity, and will run across TV, BVOD, social and radio in the UK from 7th August. The campaign was developed with Zenith, which led media planning and buying. Together, the team delivered an integrated campaign with an effective media mix, designed to elevate the Just Use Confused.com platform and build fame nationwide. It’s almost impossible to pick a favourite, but Angry Cow has to take the top spot. He was inspired by Mark from Peep Show, while the pig took plenty of cues from Jeremy. We even snuck in Mark’s iconic creamy elephant sofa and named the characters Mark Cowigan, Jeremy UsPork and Super Lamb. If you’re familiar with Peep Show, you’ll understand why. If you’re not… go and watch Peep Show. This  professional campaign titled 'Feels like…' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Confused.com, by ad agency: Leo UK. This Film and Integrated media campaign is related to the Insurance industry and contains 3 media assets. It was submitted 3 days ago.

description: Cornett Launches ‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism VisitLEX invites visitors to for a “grounding” wellness experience they can only get in Lexington, KY on the “best ground in the world” Wellness seekers are spending thousands on retreats, cold plunges, and longevity supplements. Lexington, Kentucky has a simpler suggestion: touch grass. Specifically, Bluegrass. In collaboration with long-time partner Cornett, VisitLEX, the Lexington Convention and Visitors Bureau, today launches Bluegrass Bathing, a new destination-wide wellness experience that invites locals and visitors to kick off their shoes, settle into Lexington's iconic Bluegrass landscape and reconnect with nature. The concept draws inspiration from the growing popularity of “grounding,” also known as “earthing,” a wellness practice centered on making direct contact with the Earth's surface, allowing the body to absorb its natural electrical charge. According to recent medical reports, this connection can help improve sleep, lower stress levels, and reduce inflammation. “You can sit on the ground anywhere. But there’s something special about sitting on the same earth that nourishes the world’s best Thoroughbreds,” said Jonathon Spalding, Group Creative Director at Cornett. “Why touch regular boring grass when you can touch Bluegrass?” As the Horse Capital of the World, visitors are surrounded by more than 450 horse farms. Set among the rolling hills and lush green spaces that define Kentucky's Bluegrass Region, Bluegrass Bathing transforms one of Lexington's most recognizable natural assets into an immersive wellness experience. "If grounding is all about reconnecting with the Earth, then we're inviting folks to start their wellness journey with the best, most natural and nutrient-rich ground in America," said Mary Quinn Ramer, President of VisitLEX. "For centuries, these rolling hills have nurtured some of the world's most celebrated Thoroughbreds and the limestone water that runs beneath it has become the bedrock of our bourbon industry. But it’s also the way this Bluegrass makes you feel. Visitors consistently report they feel more relaxed the moment they touch down in Lexington. Bluegrass Bathing is our invitation to slow down, take a breath and experience the landscape that makes Lexington unlike anywhere else in the world." Visitors can “Bluegrass Bathe” at some of Lexington’s most iconic outdoor spaces, including a selection of Visit Horse Country farms and a handful of Lexington’s scenic parks (including Kentucky Horse Park, Gatton Park, and designated Parks & Rec locations). By booking at participating locations, guests will receive access to a series of curated wellness experiences including Pilates and sound baths along with a selection of guided meditations designed specifically for the program. Additionally, guests can deepen their connection to the Bluegrass by booking a dedicated tour of their host farm after the bathing experience. Each of the guided meditations was inspired by the natural elements that shape Lexington's landscape, encouraging participants to slow down, engage their senses and connect with their surroundings. VisitLEX has also produced a guided Sound Bath video set amidst a local horse farm and led by Amy Hudson, a certified Reiki master and sound healer from the Sound Healing Center of Lexington. To celebrate the launch, VisitLEX has also released a promotional video inspired by luxury wellness retreats. The video follows a solitary Bluegrass Bather enjoying a lush field of Bluegrass while a soothing narrator extols the virtues of one of Kentucky's most abundant natural resources. "We love creating experiences that could only happen in Lexington," added Ramer. "Bluegrass Bathing playfully reminds travelers that sometimes the best reset is simply being present and reconnecting our bodies with the Earth in a beautiful, natural setting. It's wellness, Kentucky-style." Visitors can learn more about Bluegrass Bathing at VisitLEX.com/Bluegrass-Bathing, where they can access all of the guided meditations, explore participating locations and discover additional wellness experiences throughout the destination. This  professional campaign titled '‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: VisitLEX, by ad agency: CORNETT. video_title: American Pecan Promotion Board — “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans”
description: The American Pecan Promotion Board (APPB) is bringing back its “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans” campaign for a third round, once again teaming with ad agency Signal Theory and creative studio SixTwentySix. The new spots keep the campaign’s signature comedy going, highlighting the everyday moments when pecans are the right call. The third installment of “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans” features three spots built around everyday moments when a pecan snack becomes essential: “Move In”: A father drops his daughter off at college for an emotional goodbye, both wishing Mom could be there. She is, as it turns out, in the car the whole time snacking on pecans. “Drop Off”: A mother tries to get her son to school on time, only to be stopped by a crossing guard who takes pecan snacking very seriously. “Snack Break” (to debut later in 2026): A group of office coworkers speculate about a colleague’s frequent trips outside, unaware she is sneaking away for a pecan fix. “This year we pushed the snack break to feel less casual and a lot more urgent. It’s that moment when you need a snack before you break, and we’ve all been there,” said Joe Wilper, executive creative director at Signal Theory. “The spots lean fully into pecans as the healthy escape you needed at exactly the right moment. Whether it’s the long wait at school pickup, college move-in day or the excuse to finally get up from your desk, we’re reminding people that reaching for pecans is the smart snack in surprising moments.” The new spots mark the third collaboration between Signal Theory and SixTwentySix, led by director Evan Bourque. The partnership has grown tighter with each round, with Signal Theory crediting close creative alignment between both teams for keeping production efficient and the work sharp. "Our goal with these spots was to make them feel like snippets from a movie rather than a commercial, so every choice, from casting to locations to lighting, was built around that idea," said Evan Bourque, director at SixTwentySix. "It's always a pleasure working with the creatives at Signal Theory. They write fun scripts and stay open to new ideas, which makes the end result stronger. The characters are really what make these spots stand out, a quirky character paired with a grounded one, keeping things entertaining." This  professional campaign titled '“Surprisingly Snackable Pecans”' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: American Pecan Promotion Board, by ad agency: Signal Theory. This Digital and Film media campaign is related to the Food industry and contains 2 media assets. It was submitted 3 days ago.

description: Canva has launched its first large-scale brand campaign in Thailand, ‘Anyone Can with Canva’, positioning AI-powered video editing as an accessible tool for everyday creativity rather than a skill reserved for professional filmmakers or agencies. Created in partnership with acclaimed Thai filmmaker Nawapol Thamrongrattanarit, the campaign reflects the growing influence of short-form video across Southeast Asia and encourages a wider range of people to participate in visual storytelling. The hero film takes place inside a chaotic advertising agency struggling through endless client revisions before an unlikely group of editors, including a delivery rider, security guard and cleaner, step in to transform the project using Canva’s video editing tools. With its humorous and distinctly local tone, the campaign embraces the idea that creativity can come from anyone, regardless of professional experience, and highlights how technology is lowering barriers to content creation. A key element of the initiative is giving the public access to licensed footage from Thamrongrattanarit’s personal archive, allowing users to experiment with professional-quality material using Canva’s AI-powered editing tools and templates. The campaign also supports Canva’s broader growth strategy in Thailand, where the company has expanded its presence through partnerships such as its education initiative with the Office of the Basic Education Commission, helping bring Canva for Education to millions of students and teachers across the country. This  professional campaign titled 'Anyone Can' was published in Thailand in June, 2026. It was created for the brand: Canva Thailand, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. video_title: Pruksa — The Most Valuable Gadget in the World
description: Wolf BKK has partnered with Pruksa to launch an unconventional campaign for the property developer’s new premium residences by presenting a home as if it were the world’s most valuable gadget. Priced at 25 million baht, the campaign taps into society’s fascination with new technology, suggesting that the greatest innovation in improving everyday life may not be a device at all, but a thoughtfully designed home. The campaign began by teasing a mysterious premium gadget through billboards, digital screens, social media and online films, promoting it as a breakthrough invention with life-changing capabilities. As curiosity grew, audiences speculated that the product could be an advanced AI system or another futuristic technology capable of justifying its multimillion-baht price tag. The final reveal showed that the advertised features had never belonged to a gadget, but were the everyday benefits of a home. By disguising a premium residence as a piece of cutting-edge technology, Pruksa reframed its property launch as a conversation about value, challenging people’s obsession with the latest innovations while reminding them that a home remains one of the most meaningful investments in making life easier, smarter and more comfortable. This  professional campaign titled 'The Most Valuable Gadget in the World' was published in Thailand in July, 2026. It was created for the brand: Pruksa, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. description: Today, The Coca‑Cola Company announces the launch of ‘Fizz or Sizz’, a playful, insight‑led campaign that transforms a familiar sensory moment into a mass participation experience. Set in Japan, where fried chicken is hugely popular but not instinctively paired with Coca‑Cola, the campaign is built around a simple but surprising truth: the sound of Coca‑Cola fizzing is almost indistinguishable from the sound of karaage sizzling. By making sound the creative hero, ‘Fizz or Sizz’ turns this uncanny similarity into a nationwide guessing game — asking people one deceptively simple question: is it sizz or fizz? Rolling out across radio, digital out‑of‑home and social media, the campaign invites audiences to listen and engage in real time. Correct guesses can reward participation with a chance to win a free Coke, daily over the course of the week‑long activation. Rather than delivering a traditional product message, ‘Fizz or Sizz’ uses play, sound and immediacy to draw people into a broader cultural conversation about food, taste and refreshment. By gamifying the fizz of Coca‑Cola and placing it alongside the sizzle of freshly cooked food, the campaign subtly rewires cultural associations — making the two sensations feel inseparable in people’s minds. The activation also demonstrates how mass media can feel participatory at scale. Across radio, outdoor and social channels, audiences are invited to actively take part rather than passively observe, creating a shared moment that feels intuitive, accessible and highly shareable. Tish Condeno, Senior Director, Coca‑Cola Trademark Category, Coca‑Cola Japan said: “Sound has a way of triggering recognition in an instant. ‘Fizz or Sizz’ brings together two familiar noises that often blur together, inviting you to listen closely to the crackle of food and the first response of a drink opening or being poured. The result is a light, interactive moment for Coke lovers rooted in food and refreshment.” ‘Fizz or Sizz’ will run across Japan via radio, OOH, social and in‑store engagement touchpoints. The campaign was developed by WPP Open X, led by Grey, supported by Ogilvy, WPP Production, and WPP Media. This  professional campaign titled 'Fizz or Sizz' was published in Japan in April, 2026.
